title: How Conversion Therapy Doesn't Work
summary: Josh and Chuck examine conversion therapy (also called reparative therapy or ex-gay therapy), tracing its history from 19th-century hypnosis and aversion treatments through the American Psychological Association's 1973 declassification of homosexuality, the Christian right's adoption of the ex-gay movement, and Joseph Nicolosi's reparative therapy. They cover the damage documented by the APA and other bodies, high-profile ex-gay figures who later reversed course (John Paulk, Michael Johnston, Ted Haggard, Alan Chambers and Exodus International), the George Rekers case, and state and court actions banning the practice for minors. The episode opens with a few announcements for the live show and closes with a listener mail segment about the indefinite article "an" before "historic."
topics: electroconvulsive therapy and lobotomy in conversion therapy
state bans on conversion therapy for minors

segments.title: Live show announcement and opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts announce San Francisco Sketch Fest live show dates and tickets, then introduce the episode topic and a listener's suggestion to examine media even-handedness.

segments.title: Definition and early history of conversion therapy
segments.summary: The hosts define conversion therapy, reparative therapy and ex-gay therapy, note its ties to the Christian right, and trace 19th-century origins including a German hypnotist's claimed 1899 case, and early harmful techniques like testicular transplantation and aversion treatments.

segments.title: Psychology's shift away from treating homosexuality as disorder
segments.summary: Early practitioners included psychologists and medical doctors. The APA removed homosexuality as a mental disorder in 1973, and the field largely abandoned conversion efforts, which then revived in the 1980s with the Christian right.

segments.title: Joseph Nicolosi's reparative therapy method
segments.summary: Joseph Nicolosi's approach, based on the claim that same-sex attraction stems from childhood factors and a domineering mother and passive father triad. The hosts critique the extrapolation from a Minnesota adolescent sexuality study and describe his four-step method.

segments.title: Christian right, masculinity and the ex-gay movement
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Christian right's framing of feminism and homosexuality as signs of decadence, the emphasis on masculinity and passive fathers, and the shift toward accepting gay people who refrain from sex. They also weigh how to judge Nicolosi personally.

segments.title: What conversion therapy looks like in practice
segments.summary: Accounts of harmful practices, including a teen forced to wear a weighted backpack and a faked funeral, and secular-seeming programs teaching masculinity skills. Approximately 700,000 American adults reportedly underwent conversion therapy. The hosts also mention exorcism-style sessions.

segments.title: George Rekers case and childhood gender nonconformity
segments.summary: The hosts describe a 1974 case by psychologist George Rekers involving a four-and-a-half-year-old boy showing feminine behavior, in which the mother was trained to reward masculine behavior and punish feminine behavior. The boy later died by suicide at age thirty.

segments.title: APA task force findings on health risks
segments.summary: The 2009 APA task force concluded sexual orientation change efforts pose critical health risks. The hosts list associated harms, including depression, substance abuse and suicidality, and note that LGBTQ teens who underwent conversion therapy were three times as likely to attempt suicide.

segments.title: High-profile ex-gay figures who reversed course
segments.summary: The hosts recount the Exodus International ad campaign and Newsweek cover featuring John and Anne Paulk, John Paulk's 2000 photo outside a Washington gay bar, Michael Johnston's HIV case, Ted Haggard's scandals and 2011 bisexual admission, and Alan Chambers shutting down Exodus International with an apology.

segments.title: Legal bans on conversion therapy and court challenges
segments.summary: As of 2019, eighteen states, Washington D.C. and Puerto Rico have enacted bans, mostly covering minors and licensed professionals. The hosts discuss the Jonah counseling case in New Jersey, free speech challenges, New York City's repealed ban, and a pending Supreme Court question.

segments.title: Listener mail on the indefinite article and sign-off
segments.summary: A listener complains about the use of 'an historic' versus 'a historic'; the hosts discuss the rule, then sign off with contact and social information.
